transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Owen Mitchell (Redwood SE), Jade Kim (Redwood CSM); Mark Chen (Orion Eng), Priya Rao (Orion Head of ML), Sarah Lee (Orion CTO)

Summary:
Quick scoping of POC timeline and milestones for Orion Tech evaluating Redwood inference for production chat and embedding workloads. Covered success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark approach, security/access steps and proposed milestones: kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout. Agreed to send SOW and benchmark plan; kickoff week of 2026-03-09.

Topics:
- Success criteria: latency P95, cost targets, quality metrics on prompt set, throughput/QPS
- Workload sizing: QPS, sequence length distribution, embedding volume
- Benchmarks: synthetic vs replay, expected metrics, pass/fail thresholds
- Timeline & milestones: kickoff, access provisioning, mid-point review, final exec readout
- Security/ops: VPC peering, SSO/SAML, SOC2, audit logs, KMS

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um I think we have about an hour, maybe a bit more to cover the POC timeline and milestones. quick intros?
[00:12] Mark: Hi I'm Mark Chen, engineering lead on search and embeddings at Orion.
[00:17] Priya: Priya Rao, head of ML, I'll own success criteria and evaluation.
[00:21] Sarah: Sarah Lee, CTO, I'll be joining the exec readout.
[00:26] Lena: Great, from Redwood I'm Lena, AE, with Owen who's our solutions engineer and Jade on customer success.
[00:33] Owen: Hey everyone.

[00:35] Lena: High level — Orion is evaluating Redwood for two primary workloads: 1) conversational/chat generation for customer support with strict latency needs; 2) embeddings for semantic search across 10s of millions of docs. We want to outline a POC that proves economics and latency at scale, with clear milestones. Does that match your internal goal?
[01:00] Priya: Yep exactly, the embedding scale is the bigger unknown for us, and we also need to make sure the chat latency at p95 is under 400ms for median-ish prompts.
[01:10] Mark: To add, our current infra is a mix of managed endpoints and some in-house Triton. We're trying to reduce costs and simplify ops.

[01:22] Owen: Cool. Quick clarifying question on QPS for chat — are you expecting bursty traffic or steady state?
[01:29] Priya: Both. Production target is ~200 rps steady with bursts to 1k for short periods, average seq length 200 tokens. For embeddings we expect ~50k requests per day, batchable.

[01:45] Owen: That's helpful. For the POC we'll recommend two benchmark tracks: an inferenced latency track for chat at target QPS and sequence profile; and an embedding throughput/cost track where we replay batches. We'll run both against a Redwood-hosted test cluster (hosted) and optionally a dedicated instance if you'd like dedicated pools.
[02:10] Sarah: We care about security too — we need SOC2 report, SSO, audit logs, and ability to use our KMS. Also data residency might matter for certain datasets.

[02:25] Lena: Absolutely — we'll share the security pack. For the POC we can provision a VPC connector or private deployment if the sensitivity requires it; typically POC starts on hosted with a private VPC peering option during the access phase.

[02:40] Mark: Timeline — what's realistic? We have an internal exec review window late April, so prefer POC done by mid-April.
[02:49] Lena: Okay that gives us about six weeks. Proposed milestones:
  - Kickoff: week of 2026-03-09 (intro, access, datasets)
  - Access setup & provisioning: 1 week after kickoff (keys, VPC, sample data ingestion)
  - Baseline benchmarking (week 2-3): run synthetic & replay tests, initial tuning
  - Mid-point review: ~3 weeks in (progress, preliminary numbers, any blockers)
  - Optimization & final benchmarking (weeks 4-5)
  - Exec readout: mid-April (final results, cost model, recommendations)

[03:40] Priya: That sounds good, is that assuming hosted or dedicated? If we need dedicated GPUs for throughput tests we'll need longer lead time for capacity reservations.
[03:50] Owen: Good point. For dedicated reserved capacity we typically need a 2–3 week lead for guaranteed throughput depending on GPU type. For initial validation we can run on hosted and then switch to a short reserved window for the high-QPS run.

[04:05] Mark: For embeddings, we also need to validate incremental indexing latency. Can that be covered?
[04:11] Owen: Yes, we'll include an embedding indexing workload: small batches every minute and a bulk backfill. We'll capture per-batch latency and cost per 1M embeddings.

[04:25] Lena: Let's talk success criteria — Priya, you mentioned p95 < 400ms for chat. What else?
[04:32] Priya: Quality: model output must meet our evaluation suite thresholds (we'll share prompt set and evaluation script). Cost: target 30% lower than our current infra per-1000 tokens for chat and embeddings cost within our budget. Reliability: no more than 0.5% error/retry rate during 24h sustained run.

[04:56] Owen: We'll instrument traces and token-level cost breakdowns in the Redwood console and export metrics to your prometheus if you want.

[05:06] Mark: For the benchmarks can you run both synthetic and replay? We have a replay cluster for real user traces.
[05:12] Owen: Yes — recommend doing synthetic first to validate config, then run a replay to get production-like numbers. We can provide scripts to replay requests preserving timing.

[05:25] Sarah: Regarding compliance, will we get raw logs for audit? We need audit trails for the exec readout.
[05:31] Lena: Yes, audit logs are available; we can configure retention and export. KMS integration for keys is supported on Private/Dedicated deployments. We'll include that in the security appendix.

[05:45] Priya: What about quantization/accuracy tradeoffs? If we push quantized models the quality changes—we need to track that as part of evaluation.
[05:53] Owen: We'll include quantization profiles as one of the optimization knobs and measure quality regressions with your eval suite. We'll note which runs used which quantization level.

[06:06] Mark: Who's responsible for dataset ingestion? We prefer to provide an S3 bucket; will you pull it or do we push?
[06:14] Owen: Either works. For hosted test runs we typically provide temporary signed URLs and we pull into a test bucket; for private deployments we'll arrange a direct S3 role or VPC access.

[06:25] Lena: Ok let's anchor milestones with owners and dates — kickoff 2026-03-09. Action items we'll capture in the notes and follow up by email.

[06:36] Owen: Benchmarks plan — we'll run two passes: baseline (no caching, default batching) then optimized (caching, tuned batching, quantization if acceptable). We'll record latency distribution, QPS, GPU utilization, and cost per token/embedding.

[06:55] Mark: For embeddings cost per 1M is critical. We have current numbers — I'll share them so you can compare apples-to-apples.

[07:03] Priya: Exec readout — we'd like a short 20-minute deck focusing on top-line numbers, cost delta, risk, recommendations. Sarah will attend plus two directors.

[07:15] Sarah: Yes, and please surface any operational gaps we should be aware of for production.

[07:22] Owen: We'll prepare an ops checklist covering autoscaling, fallback policies, and monitoring hooks for your SREs.

[07:30] Lena: Timing for SOW — we'll get that to you by EOD 2026-03-05. The SOW will include scope, timeline, responsibilities, and optional dedicated capacity pricing.

[07:40] Mark: Sounds good. On data residency — a subset of our data must remain in EU. Can you support a region-limited POC?
[07:49] Owen: Yes; we can pin the test cluster to eu-west region for the runs and show regional routing. That will be in the access checklist.

[08:00] Priya: For success criteria — one more point: embedding recall@10 should be at least 0.78 on our test set. We'll provide the eval scripts.

[08:09] Owen: Noted. We'll add that as a pass/fail metric for embedding track.

[08:15] Jade: On the CSM side I'll coordinate the kickoff and calendar invites and make sure we have the right participants for the mid-point review.

[08:23] Lena: Great. Any blockers we should call out now?
[08:27] Mark: We need temporary API access and a place to host the sample dataset; I'll try to send both by 2026-03-04.
[08:34] Priya: Also need confirmation on whether we'll do a dedicated short window for the 1k burst test — that affects capacity booking.

[08:42] Owen: We'll provision hosted and if you confirm dedicated test we'll put in a capacity reservation for the burst window; note that may add cost.

[08:50] Sarah: Budget-wise we'll want a clear cost model in the SOW.

[08:54] Lena: We'll include a cost projection and a comparison to your current numbers once you share them.

[09:00] (brief cross-talk and clarifications)

[09:20] Owen: Ok summary of technical milestones we'll include in the SOW:
  - Kickoff + access (2026-03-09) — Orion provides dataset and access, Redwood provisions test cluster
  - Baseline benchmark (wk1-2) — synthetic runs, initial numbers
  - Mid-point review (~week3) — preliminary latency/cost, blockers
  - Dedicated capacity test (optional, week4) — high-burst validation
  - Final benchmarking + exec readout (mid-April)

[09:55] Priya: That aligns with our internal calendar.

[10:00] Lena: Next steps recap: Lena sends SOW by 2026-03-05, Owen sends benchmark scripts by 2026-03-06, Mark to provide dataset and QPS targets by 2026-03-04, Jade to schedule kickoff for week of 2026-03-09.

[10:20] Mark: I'll also put together current cost numbers for chat and embeddings.

[10:28] Priya: I'll confirm the eval scripts and expected thresholds.

[10:33] Sarah: We'll be at the exec readout unless something changes.

[10:38] Lena: Any final questions?

[10:41] Mark: None from me.

[10:43] Priya: All good.

[10:45] Lena: Great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the SOW and the security pack.

[10:50] Owen: Thanks all.

[11:00] End meeting.
